note: Courts that take C100 and FL401 applications only through the online portal, never by email. Case flow drafts no court email for a matter at one of these; a person files through the portal and marks it filed. 'match' holds the distinctive words of the court's name, matched as whole words in order (so 'hull' is never 'Solihull').

call_first.name: Birmingham
call_first.note: Mon to Fri 9am to 5pm; slots 10:00 to 12:30, at most 3 per firm per day. Then send the application to familyapplications.birmingham.countycourt@justice.gov.uk at least 1 hour before the slot. The court's own email says a paper hearing and no attendance; its guidance sheet says attend 30 minutes early: the court's own email decides.

slow.name: Stockport
slow.note: Rarely answers a without-notice application without a nudge.

slow_note: Courts that rarely respond without a nudge. After nudge_working_days working days with no reply to a without-notice application, the court-reply to-do is made with a suggested chase email (never sent). It stops mattering once the court has given a hearing date and case number. 'match' works as for the portal list.
call_first_note: Courts that return a without-notice application unissued unless a hearing slot is booked by phone first. Case flow still drafts the email normally; it only tells a person to call, in the Case flow step and the bell. 'match' works as for the portal list.
